What is Genasys and what does it do? Genasys is cloud-based insurance software that brings policy administration , claims management and billing together in a single platform. It is built for insurers, MGAs and brokers managing delegated authority, with no-code product building tools, 350+ pre-configured templates and 450+ documented API endpoints . Genasys is headquartered in London with offices in South Africa, and has been serving the insurance industry for nearly 30 years. The platform is used by enterprise carriers transacting hundreds of millions in GWP and scaling MGAs launching new products in days. Genasys has been recognised by Celent, CNBC & Statista and BusinessCloud as one of the leading insurance technology platforms in the world. How long does implementation take, and how disruptive is migration from our legacy system? Implementation timelines depend on product complexity, integrations and data migration scope, but the platform is configured rather than heavily customised, which reduces delivery risk and time. Genasys delivered Arma Karma's policy administration platform in one week and King Price migrated from legacy technology in six weeks , though more complex environments will naturally take longer. Migration is handled through structured data import routines and reconciliation checks to ensure accuracy, with the option to phase deployment by product, entity or distribution channel. This staged approach allows organisations to transition gradually and avoid operational disruption during the move from legacy systems. What types of insurance business does Genasys support? Genasys is used by insurers, MGAs, brokers and third-party administrators across personal, commercial and specialty lines. The platform supports complex insurance structures including multi-currency, multi-jurisdictional tax, co-insurance, capacity splits and delegated authority arrangements. Customers range from startup MGAs launching their first product to established carriers managing large, complex books across multiple regions. Current clients include Simplyhealth, King Price , Hamilton, Guardrisk, Arma Karma , CTU and BSpoke Group, among others. How does Genasys integrate with our existing technology ecosystem? Genasys is built on an open API architecture with more than 450 documented RESTful API endpoints . External systems can create, read and update platform data across policy , claims and billing modules. This enables integration with pricing engines, CRM systems, general ledgers, premium finance providers, data enrichment services, payment platforms and distribution channels. Genasys also supports real-time eventing and automated B2B data feeds, removing the need for manual bordereaux processing. Clients retain their existing technology ecosystem while using Genasys as the core operational system. What does it actually cost, and how does total cost of ownership compare to legacy platforms? Pricing is based on factors including users, transaction volumes, integrations and migration scope. Genasys is priced for the mid-market but delivers enterprise-grade capability, which means organisations get the depth of functionality they would expect from a tier-one platform without the corresponding cost structure. Because the platform is cloud-based and configured rather than custom-developed, total cost of ownership is typically lower than legacy alternatives. Clients reduce infrastructure overhead, eliminate custom development cycles and lower ongoing operational administration.
